statement.p: A rectangular swimming pool 70 ft long, 15 ft wide, and 10 ft deep is filled with water to a depth of 8 ft. Use an integral to find the work required to pump all the water out over the top. (Take as the density of water \delta = 62.4 \hbox{lb/ft}^3.)

static.solution:
h ft above the bottom, a slice of thickness \Delta h has \hbox{Volume }\approx 70\cdot 15\Delta h \hbox{ ft}{}^3. Since the density of water is \rho lb/ft{}^3, \hbox{Weight of the slice }\approx\rho(70 \cdot 15 \cdot \Delta h) \hbox{ lbs}. The distance to lift the slice of water at height h ft is 10 - h ft, so the work to move one slice, \Delta W, is \Delta W = \rho \cdot \hbox{Volume} \cdot \hbox{Distance lifted} \approx \rho(70 \cdot 15 \cdot \Delta h)(10 - h) = 1050 \rho (10 - h) \Delta h\hbox{ ft-lb}.
The work done, W, to pump all the water is the sum of the work done on the pieces: W \approx \Sigma\, 1050 \rho(10-h)\Delta h. As \Delta h \rightarrow 0, we obtain a definite integral. Since h varies from h = 0 to h = 8 and \rho=62.4\hbox{ lb/ft}{}^3, the total work is: W = \int_0^{8} 65520 (10-h)dh = 65520 \left(10 h - {h^2\over 2}\right)\bigg|_0^{8} = 65520 (48) = 3144960\, \hbox{lbf}.
